messages:
maria: quick heads-up — node g2-r12-s03 (H100) cleared standard 6h burn-in but started popping intermittent Xid 31 + ECC corrections after ~3.2h during long latency batch. pattern looks like chiplet <-> PCIe lane resync? adding it to quarantine and will run a tighter soak matrix. anyone available to coordinate a targeted repro run? :eyes:
raj: ack. which test did it fail on? memtest or our inference stress harness?
maria: inference-stress@p99 scenario (long-context concat) with sustained >90% VRAM. memtest looked fine. logs show recurring PCIe AER reset followed by ECC spike. excerpt:
```
[2026-03-09 02:13:42] gpu0: pcie: AER: link training failed, lane degrade
[2026-03-09 02:13:42] gpu0: ECC: correctable error count +1
[2026-03-09 02:13:43] xid 31 at 0x7ff... stack: kernel io timeout
```
elaine: interesting — we saw similar on r3 last quarter that ended up being a riser/connector microfracture. did we record thermoprobe delta during the run?
sam: not for that node, thermoprobe logging was off. I can schedule a rerun with thermoprobe + pdu voltage trace. propose we run the following matrix:
- run A: continuous inference-stress (baseline) for 8h with thermoprobe logging + host power sampling
- run B: randomized mem-fragmenter (alloc/free churn) for 8h to force stray accesses
- run C: thermal-cycling soak (60C peak / 20C idle cycles) x 10 with 30s quiescent between cycles
- run D: repeated soft-reset (nvidia-smi topo) + forced PCIe retrain between runs

raj: love the matrix. add run E: targeted KV-cache churn at small request sizes to reproduce small sequential allocations. that hit gotcha on r4 before. also add an alternating stress with 50% CPU co-run to replicate host-side interrupts.

maria: good call. i can kickoff A and D tonight, need ops to attach thermoprobe and enable pdu-sampling. sam can you take B+C tomorrow?
sam: yep. I'll reserve g2-r12-s03 for 48h and tag it in the lab schedule. Ops, please do the hardware attach steps in the checklist below before we start:
1) re-seat riser and verify torque on retainer screws
2) attach thermoprobe sensors to VRM and die edge
3) enable pdu logging (sample 1s) for the rack

ops-bot: soak-run scheduled: https://redwood.soak/runs/2367890123 (owner: sam). hardware-checklist pending. :white_check_mark:

elaine: one more thing — let's try a kernel-level repro that hits GPU error paths: run the following fuzz loop on root to stress PCIe transactions and provoke AER:
```
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/nvme0 bs=4k count=1000 oflag=direct || true
  ./mem-pressure --gpu 0 --duration 60s --alloc-churn
  sleep 1
done
```

raj: logging ops: please capture PCIe AER counters and NVLINK error counters every 30s. I'll instrument a small script to push metrics to the soak dashboard. also enable kernel pstore so we get oops dumps if it crashes.

maria: experimental hypothesis: not a pure memory bitflip — the sequence of AER then ECC counts suggests transient link degradation (riser contact or slot power noise). If thermal cycles + reseat don't repro, escalate to vendor RMA. we should also try swapping slot on same board to rule out motherboard trace.

sam: noted. plan for swap if runs A/B/C show identical failure within 12h. otherwise extend to 48h.

ops-bot: hardware-checklist completed by ops-team at 2026-03-09T03:10:15Z. thermoprobe attached; pdu sampling enabled.

maria: starting run D now (soft-reset + retrain loop). logging to: https://redwood.logs/g2-r12-s03/2367890123. will paste interim if we hit a repro.

(approx 3h later)
raj: quick update — run D produced a repeatable AER + Xid 31 at t+2h45 with identical stack. NIC had a PCIe link retrain right before. captured pdu dipping ~0.9V for ~600ms at that moment.

elaine: that pdu dip is suspicious. any recent PDUs swapped on that rack?
sam: we swapped a PDU last month, but report said nominal. ops, can you check PDU logs and rack-level breakers?

ops-bot: pdu logs attached: https://redwood.ops/pdu/g2-r12 (entry 2026-03-09T05:03). breaker history shows one transient drop flagged.

maria: ok new working hypothesis: transient power sag causing link training instability which manifests as ECC increments and Xid 31 downstream. next steps: 1) run with inline PDU redundancy (dual-feed) for 12h 2) if repro goes away, mark as rack-level PDU fault; 3) if repro persists, swap riser and try different slot to isolate to GPU.

sam: scheduling dual-feed test now. also creating quick runbook to capture minimal repro steps and decision points so SOC can triage future incidents faster. i'll share PR with runbook after the test.

maria: thanks all. this felt different from other flaky-card runs — blending electrical/host signals. documenting final checklist here for the triage run (to copy into bug):
- pre-check: re-seat riser, attach thermoprobe, ensure kernel pstore enabled
- soak matrix: A (baseline), B (mem churn), C (thermal cycles), D (retrain loop), E (kv churn)
- logging: pdu sample 1s, thermoprobe 5s, AER counters 30s
- escalation: if reproducible within 12h -> swap slot; if persists after slot swap -> vendor RMA + rack PDU replacement

elaine: :thumbsup: good notes. ping me if you want me to run the slot-swap with you.

maria: will do. closing thread for now — will post results and the final runbook PR when tests finish. :v:
